lines.text: San Francisco rent is nearly 3x the US median. Why?
lines.say: San Francisco rent is nearly triple the US median. Why?

lines.text: Median one-bedroom rent, Sept 2026: $4,400 in SF vs $1,518 nationwide, per Zumper.
lines.say: In September twenty twenty-six, Zumper's median one-bedroom was four thousand four hundred dollars in San Francisco, versus fifteen hundred eighteen nationwide.

lines.text: Rent is just a price: people who want homes vs homes that exist.
lines.say: Rent is a price: people who want homes, versus homes that exist.

lines.text: Demand first. San Francisco's one-bedroom rent rose 25.4% in a year, and Zumper ties that to AI hiring.
lines.say: Demand first. San Francisco's one-bedroom rent rose twenty-five point four percent in a year, and Zumper ties that to AI hiring.

lines.text: Supply: San Francisco County permitted 2,519 homes in 2021 and just 770 in 2024 (Census).
lines.say: Then supply. San Francisco County permitted two thousand five hundred nineteen homes in twenty twenty-one, and just seven hundred seventy in twenty twenty-four.

lines.text: Zoning rules, like height limits, shape what gets built. And land near jobs is pricey.
lines.say: Zoning rules, like height limits, shape what gets built. And land near jobs is pricey.

lines.text: Compare Houston: its whole metro area permitted 65,075 homes in 2025 (Census).
lines.say: Compare Houston, whose whole metro area permitted sixty-five thousand seventy-five homes in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: So high rent usually means well-paid jobs chasing too few homes.

post.title: Why a San Francisco 1BR rents for nearly 3x the US median
post.ig:
Why does a San Francisco one-bedroom rent for nearly 3x the US median?
Median 1BR rent, Sept 2026: $4,400 in San Francisco vs $1,518 nationwide, per Zumper.
SF rent rose 25.4% in a year as AI hiring added demand. SF County permitted just 770 homes in 2024, down from 2,519 in 2021.
Houston's whole metro area permitted 65,075 homes in 2025, second most in the US.
Sources: Zumper National Rent Report, US Census Bureau building permits (via FRED).
